text:
aria: FYI customer BlueWave reporting console usage charts lagging ~6 hours after the large backfill last night. Ticket BW-482 attached. Can someone take lead?

morgan: I'm on it. Quick check of consumer groups shows heavy lag on `console-hourly-rollup-consumer` (~2.3M messages). Suspect backfill flood caused reordering + throttling.

aria: Backfill job id: backfill-20260316-23. Backfill-bot showed status: SUCCESS but with warnings (S3 eventual consistency warnings).

backfill-bot: job backfill-20260316-23 finished. warnings: ["s3_put_retry: 12", "manifest-write-delay: 00:40"].

devon: Can you paste the consumer lag output?

morgan: Sure, from kafka-monitor:
``` 
Group: console-hourly-rollup-consumer
Partition: 12 Lag: 1_200_345
Partition: 13 Lag: 980_102
Total lag: 2_345_678
Last commit: 2026-03-16T23:45:12Z
```

morgan: Also seeing many retry rate spikes in the worker logs: `ERROR consumer: offset out of range` followed by fast restarts.

sam: Two possible vectors: 1) manifest propagation to rollup workers delayed -> workers not seeing new objects; 2) consumer commit thrash causing reprocessing slowdown. I lean toward manifest delay because backfill-bot had `manifest-write-delay`.

aria: BlueWave is complaining charts are stale; they need accurate hourly totals for last 12 hours. SLA is 4 hours. We're beyond that.

devon: Quick repro to check visibility: run the read query against raw bucket and compare to materialized view. Example:
```
aws s3 ls s3://backfills/bluewave/backfill-20260316-23/ --recursive | wc -l
SELECT count(*) FROM raw_events WHERE tenant_id='bluewave' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-03-16T20:00:00Z' AND '2026-03-17T06:00:00Z';
```

morgan: Ran the S3 ls — manifest directory only populated for first 40 minutes; additional shards appeared ~00:35 UTC later than expected. That matches the manifest-write-delay.

sam: Ok that explains worker starvation; they poll the manifest and only start processing when they see files. Meanwhile, the consumer that reads the CDC topic kept trying and got into offset thrash. We'll need to: scale up rollup workers, requeue remaining offsets to earliest for the group, and run a targeted rehydrate for tenant `bluewave` for the missing window.

aria: Are there safe commands for rehydrate we can run without causing duplicate billing? We want idempotent steps.

devon: Use the rehydrate job with idempotency flag: `rehydrate --tenant bluewave --from 2026-03-16T20:00:00Z --to 2026-03-17T06:00:00Z --idempotent true --job-name manual-rehydrate-bw-1`

morgan: I'll scale workers x2 now and bump kafka consumer parallelism to 12. Running `rehydrate` after workers are up.

backfill-bot: alert: consumer-group-throttle detected; recommended action: increase consumer instances.

aria: Devon, can you prepare the SQL patch to upsert any missing hourly rows into `console_hourly_rollups` if rehydrate misses anything? Keep it scoped to tenant_id to avoid table-wide locks.

devon: Drafting now. Will use temp table + single transaction insert-on-conflict: 
```
BEGIN;
CREATE TEMP TABLE bw_missing AS
SELECT hour_bucket(ts) as hr, sum(tokens) as tokens, 'bluewave' as tenant_id
FROM raw_events
WHERE tenant_id='bluewave' AND ts >= '2026-03-16T20:00:00Z' AND ts < '2026-03-17T06:00:00Z'
GROUP BY hr;
INSERT INTO console_hourly_rollups (tenant_id, hour, tokens)
SELECT tenant_id, hr, tokens FROM bw_missing
ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, hour) DO UPDATE SET tokens = EXCLUDED.tokens;
COMMIT;
```

sam: That looks safe. We should run in read-replica first to sanity-check counts.

morgan: Workers scaled, kicking off `rehydrate` job now (manual-rehydrate-bw-1). ETA ~25m. I'll monitor consumer lag and worker logs.

aria: I'll message BlueWave with interim update: we're running a targeted rehydrate and expect charts to catch up within an hour.

morgan: Log snippet while rehydrate starting: `INFO rehydrate: discovered 128 shards to process; concurrency=24; enqueueing jobs`

morgan: 20m in — consumer lag reduced to ~150k, rollup inserts flowing.

aria: Nice. Keep an eye on duplicate counts in console. If anything looks off, pause rehydrate.

devon: I'll prep the upsert SQL and run on staging now.

morgan: Rehydrate completed for the window. Final check: hourly rows for tenant show up-to-date through 2026-03-17T05:00:00Z.

aria: I'll confirm with the customer and close BW-482 if they verify. Thanks team. :thumbsup: 

sam: Postmortem follow-ups: 1) add alert for manifest-write-delay > 5m, 2) make rehydrate idempotency default for large backfills, 3) add consumer backoff to avoid offset thrash.

aria: Assigning follow-ups to infra backlog. Closing conversation here when customer confirms.
